    Changelog

    isw 0.1.0

    Finite-line stream representation

    • Stream injection is now distributed uniformly along each stream segment using finite-line response calculations, replacing injection at discrete segment model points. This changes both constant-head injection rates and stream-induced aquifer water-level responses.
    • Constant-head boundary conditions remain imposed at segment model_point locations at each injection interval endpoint.
    • Stream segments now use stream_width instead of an effective injection-well well_diam. Width defaults to 1 m and regularizes near-stream responses using a minimum distance of half the width. Physical pumping wells continue to use well_diam.

    Function names and argument changes

    • Renamed the main workflow functions to distinguish input preparation, schedule generation, and response modeling:

      Previous function Replacement Argument changes
      get_stream_segments() prep_stream_segments() Adds stream_width = NULL.
      get_adf_stream_apportionment() prep_adf_stream_apportionment() None.
      get_adf_stream_depletion() model_adf_stream_depletion() None.
      get_stream_injection_schedule() generate_stream_injection_schedule() Requires stream_segments; replaces allow_many_aquifer_parameter_sets = FALSE with allow_n_aquifer_parameter_sets = 5; adds quadrature_order = 16L.
      get_aquifer_water_level_change() model_aquifer_water_level_change() Replaces allow_many_aquifer_parameter_sets = FALSE with allow_n_aquifer_parameter_sets = 5; adds quadrature_order = 16L.
      generate_segment_sample_points() prep_stream_sample_points() None.

    • Reversed the public injection_rate sign convention: positive values now represent water moving from the stream into the aquifer. Calculate total stream depletion with sum(injection_rate) rather than -sum(injection_rate). The water_level_change sign convention remains unchanged: negative values indicate decline.

    • In prep_stream_segments(), a supplied scalar stream_width applies to all reaches; otherwise reach-level widths are retained, defaulting to 1 m when absent. Stream-reach and stream-segment inputs no longer accept well_diam.

    • In generate_stream_injection_schedule() and model_aquifer_water_level_change(), quadrature_order controls the number of Gauss–Legendre points per straight edge of each stream segment. The default is 16.

    • The default constant-head limit changes from ten unique aquifer parameter sets to five. Set allow_n_aquifer_parameter_sets = Inf for unrestricted calculations, replacing the former allow_many_aquifer_parameter_sets = TRUE.

    • For method = "adf", generate_stream_injection_schedule() now requires stream geometry through stream_segments. Unlike the former get_stream_injection_schedule(), it does not accept an apportionment object as the third argument or recover geometry from stream_apportionment.

    • prep_adf_stream_apportionment() returns a relationship tibble without duplicated stream geometry or segment attributes. Join results to stream_segments when spatial geometry is needed.

    Schedule reuse

    • generate_stream_injection_schedule(method = "adf") now accepts partially precomputed adf_stream_depletion. Available boundary values are reused, and missing times are calculated internally with a warning.
    • Generated schedules record their injection method and quadrature order. When a constant-head schedule is supplied to model_aquifer_water_level_change(), its quadrature order is reused unless explicitly overridden. A different supplied order produces a warning.

    Other API changes

    • Renamed get_usgs_stream_reaches() to fetch_usgs_stream_reaches().

    • Renamed the specialized analytical functions:

      Previous function Replacement Argument changes
      get_stream_depletion_fraction() calc_straight_stream_depletion_fraction() Removes df; physical inputs must be supplied explicitly.
      get_aquifer_drawdown_ratio() calc_infinite_aquifer_drawdown_ratio() Removes df; physical inputs must be supplied explicitly.
      get_straight_stream_drawdown_ratio() calc_straight_stream_drawdown_ratio() Removes df; physical inputs must be supplied explicitly.

    • Removed get_stream_reach_apportionment(), get_apportioned_stream_depletion(), get_apportioned_aquifer_drawdown(), and get_depletion_from_pumping(). Use the preparation and modeling workflow above.

    • Removed the re-exported %>% operator.
